properties.headline: Tropical Storm Watch issued October 1 at 4:25AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...26W UPGRADED TO TROPICAL STORM AS IT APPROACHES THE NORTHERN
CNMI...
...TROPICAL STORM WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FOR ALAMAGAN AND PAGAN...
...TYPHOON WATCH NOW IN EFFECT FOR ALAMAGAN AND PAGAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
26W has been upgraded to a Tropical Storm.
A Tropical Storm Warning is now in effect for Alamagan and Pagan
in the CNMI.
A Typhoon Watch is now in effect for Alamagan and Pagan.
A Tropical Storm Watch remains in effect for Tinian, Saipan, and
Agrihan in the CNMI.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Tropical Storm Warning is now in effect for Alamagan and Pagan
in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch is now in effect for Alamagan and Pagan.

A Tropical Storm Watch remains in effect for Tinian, Saipan, and
adjacent coastal waters.

A Tropical Storm Watch remains in effect for Agrihan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of
74 mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.

A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the next 48 hours somewhere within the specified
areas.

A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

All persons in the watch areas should review their preparedness
plan and begin to take actions to prepare for conditions as
indicated by your local forecast and additional details, below,
for your island.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 3 AM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm 26W was located near
latitude 16.1N, longitude 150.5E. This was about 325 miles east-
northeast of Saipan, 325 miles east-southeast of Alamagan, and
420 miles east-northeast of Guam. Storm motion was west-
northwest, 285 degrees, at 5 mph. Storm intensity was 40 mph. The
current forecast track reflects an intensifying 26W will move
into the CNMI on Friday, curving north-northeast as it nears
Alamagan Friday night as a Category 1 typhoon, then pass near
Pagan and east of Agrihan Saturday.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm 26W has slowed down, and the latest forecast track
no longer reflects a full passage moving to the west of the
islands. 26W will continue west through Thursday night, making a
turn to the northwest Friday morning as it begins to approach
Alamagan from the south, turning sharply northward, then north-
northeastward late Friday night, which will bring it near Pagan
and east of Agrihan through Saturday. This sharper northward turn
will pull the tropical storm force wind field slightly further
north, with the latest forecast still including Saipan and
northern parts of Tinian briefly within the southern edge of the
TS winds. This forecasted passage over Alamagan and Pagan will
prolong the duration of damaging winds across the northern
islands, likely leading to a lengthy period of time of damaging to
destructive tropical storm conditions beginning Thursday evening
and continuing into Sunday afternoon. 26W is forecast to
strengthen to a typhoon Friday morning as it approaches Alamagan,
which would bring Alamagan, and later Pagan, directly within the
typhoon force winds Friday night through early Saturday morning.
So, a Typhoon Watch has been issued for Alamagan and Pagan, and a
Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Alamagan and Pagan.

...NEW INFORMATION...
A Coastal Flood Watch, Flash Flood Watch, and High Surf Advisory
have been issued.
properties.instruction:
Keep informed while listening for possible warnings. Secure loose
outdoor objects which can be blown around. Strongly consider
evacuating if you live in a metal roof or container home, and do
so if ordered by local officials.

Take small loose object indoors. Identify suitable shelter. Stock up
a few days worth of food and water. If no concrete shelter is
available, look for a cave or something similar. Take action to
protect food crops or other possessions as appropriate.

.WIND INFORMATION...
Northerly winds of 10 to 15 mph will turn toward the northwest,
then southwest and increase through Friday as 26W moves into the
northern CNMI and strengthens, potentially becoming a typhoon
Friday morning as it approaches Alamagan from the south. Tropical
storm force winds of 39 to 50 mph may begin by Friday morning.
Depending on the track and intensity, winds may increase to strong
tropical storm-force of 58 to 65 mph early Saturday morning.
Typhoon force winds greater than 74 mph look to remain just east
of Agrihan at this time.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Surf will initially build to 8 to 11 ft along east-facing reefs
through Friday morning, then spread along north and west-facing
reefs as the center moves north-northeast through the northern
CNMI Friday night through Saturday night, increasing to 12 to 16
ft. As 26W continues to strengthen, hazardous surf will continue
to increase. Then, as 26W begins to move away from the northern
CNMI late Saturday, surf will build by several feet along south
facing reefs as well, likely becoming hazardous. Coastal
inundation of 1 to 2 feet will be possible along all reefs.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 652 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Amarillo, Canyon, Lake Tanglewood, Mescalero Park and Timbercreek
Canyon.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 30 at 9:25PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Winds, seas, and surf will increase over the next several days as the
broad monsoon pattern surges to the south of Tropical Depression
26W, which is expected to continue to develop near the Marianas and
pass through the northern CNMI on Friday. Current guidance suggests
the highest winds and seas will initially be felt across the outer
islands between Yap and Chuuk Lagoon, as the monsoon surge develops
and shifts westward. Then, winds will increase for Palau and Yap
through the weekend leading to increasingly choppy seas, potentially
becoming hazardous to small craft late Sunday as sustained winds
increase to near 22 knots. In the meantime, moderate to fresh west
to southwest winds prevail across the region. Interisland travel
will be hazardous over the next few days. Additionally, surf will
increase along north and west-facing reefs of Yap and Chuuk,
potentially becoming hazardous this weekend. Scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms are expected over the next few days for Palau
and Yap with numerous showers developing farther north, with ensemble
model guidance showing accumulations of 1 to 3 inches possible for
Yap Island, and the outer islands of Yap and Chuuk States, and 1 to 2
inches for Palau, through the weekend.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 29 at 2:54PM PDT until October 1 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.03 ft MLLW) at 2:10 PM
Wednesday 9/30, and 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW) at 2:58
PM Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 29 at 1:45PM PDT until September 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Strong rip currents. Minor tidal overflows, especially
during the late morning high tides.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant
damage is expected. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers
out to sea.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or

Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* IMPACTS...Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant
damage is expected. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers
out to sea.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Far southeastern Elbert and southern Lincoln county.

* WHEN...From midnight MDT tonight through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A surge of tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Polo
and a storm system will bring a threat of flooding late tonight
through Thursday morning. Periods of heavy rainfall may lead to
totals of 1 to 2.5 inches in the watch area, with locally higher
amounts possible.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
